questions.q: Why does the churn service accept raw customer fields instead of pre-scaled, one-hot-encoded features?
options: The saved pipeline already contains its preprocessing, so callers only send raw columns
FastAPI cannot accept numeric features
Scaling is illegal inside a web service
Raw fields make the model more accurate
questions.explain: Because the whole pipeline was saved, preprocessing travels with the model and callers never need to know about scaling or encoding.

questions.q: Where should the model file be loaded in the service?
options: Inside the predict function on every request
Once at startup, then reused for every request
In the caller's application
Only after the first error occurs
questions.explain: Loading is much slower than predicting, so the model is loaded once when the server starts and held in memory.

questions.q: A caller sends contract = "weekly", which was never in the training data. What happens in this service?
options: The model silently predicts anyway
The server crashes
The request is rejected with HTTP 422 before it reaches the model
The contract is replaced with the most common value
questions.explain: The Pydantic Literal type only allows three contract values, so FastAPI returns a 422 validation error.

questions.q: Why include a model version in every response?
options: It makes the response larger and slower
HTTP requires a version field
It lets you trace any score back to the artifact that produced it
It replaces the need for a health endpoint
questions.explain: Versioned responses make debugging, auditing, and monitoring possible when several model versions exist over time.

questions.q: You want to rename a response field that other teams already use. What is the safest approach?
options: Rename it and tell nobody
Add the new field or publish a new API version, and keep the old contract working
Delete the old field immediately
Move the field into the request body
questions.explain: The schema is a promise to callers. Change it additively or behind a new version such as /v2/predict.
